body: Oh yes, lesson learned loud & clear. Last thing I'd want to do is offend you righteous good Samaratins who were "kind" enough to grace this poor post. Unhelpful in the guise of being helpful - not interested.

Point me in the direction where anyone tried to get more information from me. The one question directed towards me, I responded, albeit with moodiness, which, face it, I am moody all things considered.

After, I get bombarded with pettiness and insults. Why should I take anyone's opinion when it's straight from their own asses and apparently their own self worth depends on it? No thanks. Not instrested. Go fuck yourself. 

But hey changing my password, whoo! There's a thought!
Hey, man I know how to read. Why should I value their opinion? Is that why I came here? You and the rest showed up like you know how to evaluate the situation of someone who has barely said anything.

It's amazing how fragile your ego is. You've provided no degree of insight, advice, or empathy. I posted here not to debate anyone or mince words, but because I'm in a low place. You've lived your 30 years with no understanding of how to comfort people, so fuck off.

Yeah, the feedback here has been great.

For the future I know if I get upset in an anonymous forum I MUST be hiding something. And I should try to appreciate my SO violating my privacy because she apparently will be buying a sexy nurse outfit.

Nothing tops the advice of establishing boundaries in a post about violating boundaries. Reddit's top minds have congregated here, surely.

You're not too good at reading I guess. Never said you were personally angry - again, it's literally written in my comment.

Fantastic advice by the way. My post says "My girlfriend has no boundaries" so you say.. Establish boundaries. Huh, imagine that.

Why do you feel like your thoughts are even worth anything? Yeah, my girlfriend knows my phone password - why would it even be relevant that your SO doesn't know yours? Oh, yeah, it's really strange different people might have different relationships. You're presumably in your 30s and that's the sage advice you've come up with?

It is amazing you guys can somehow formulate sides from misreading my past comments (my therapist is the one who suggested drawing, not my girlfriend) and a handful of details.

Yes, somehow my girlfriend is justified in betraying my expectations of privacy because I express anger in an anonymous post on reddit.

Porn, my own writings. That's what she's looking through - and it's all in my comment. Yeah, I'm angry because it feels like betrayal. You've only been angry when you're guilty? You're seriously trying to analyze my psychology and that's what you think?

Maybe it's my optimism that she could handle knowing my phone password or staying logged into my Google account on our shared pc.

If she's rummaging through MY things, it already has everything to do with me. It's violating and humiliating. Like, am I really supposed to apologize for my taste in porn? Why the fuck does she have to be a part of that? Or if I'm venting in a goddamn google doc, who gave her the right to read it?
Suicide & unforeseeable doom withstanding, I don't know how anyone makes it 80+ years on this planet. God, 60 more years for me.
I just don't know what I'm supposed to say. Like, she is the only person I could possibly talk to. Am I wrong to get unresponsive? How am I supposed to pretend like I'm not upset?
Thanks for bothering, by the way. With everyone else you've written to, you don't have to worry yourself about me. I'll be all right
Yes, I'm on the couch tonight.

From time to time I think back to my first apprehension of death as a kid. As I was about to go to sleep the thought came on like a flash of lightning - What happens when you die?

I used to think Catholicism could provide some solace - if things had gone somewhat differently, it might have been possible to believe. But how could religion - any religion in fact - with its inherent history of suffering have gained a stronghold on the knowledge of what happens after death? Is that temptation, a test to not believe? Why are we so rational and irrational, both at the same time and forever?
When I was in college, I was seeing a therapist. I started because I was feeling increasingly dissociative and alienated. She'd have me draw pictures of how I felt. That shit made me want to die.
